fixes.explanation: I see why you'd go there, friend. The family heads do call Zelophehad "our brother." But the verse says the LORD commanded that his inheritance go to his daughters (Numbers 36:2). These men are reminding Moses of that command, not asking for the land for themselves.

I get it, friend, since the LORD commanded Moses to give the land by lot (Numbers 36:2). But Moses never tells them to trust the lot. He says, "The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks correctly." (Numbers 36:5) They aren't brushed off at all.

Yes, baker. Moses says it's because "…each of the Israelites is to retain the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers." (Numbers 36:7) So the land stays in the tribe, and it doesn't move to another one. That's the reason the text gives, plain and simple.

Good try, since the LORD commanded Moses to give the land by lot (Numbers 36:2). But Moses says nothing here about casting lots a second time. His reason is that "…each of the Israelites is to retain the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers." (Numbers 36:7)

Right, baker. The text says the five sisters "…were married to cousins on their father’s side." (Numbers 36:11) That's how they stayed within their father's tribe. Five weddings, and every one of them kept the inheritance right where it belonged. That's a full tray with no cookie out of place.
